:::{#def-strong-induction}
#### Proof by strong induction

Let $n_0$ be an [integer](number-systems.qmd#def-integers),
and let $P(n)$ be a [predicate](proof-writing.qmd#def-predicate)
about the [integers](number-systems.qmd#def-integers) $n \ge n_0$.
A **proof by strong induction**
[@wikipedia_mathematical_induction]
on $n$
shows that $P(n)$ holds for every integer $n \ge n_0$
by showing one thing:
for every integer $n \ge n_0$,
if $P(k)$ holds for every integer $k$ with $n_0 \le k < n$,
then $P(n)$ holds.

The assumption that $P(k)$ holds for every integer $k$ with $n_0 \le k < n$
is the **strong induction hypothesis**.

For $n = n_0$ no integer $k$ satisfies $n_0 \le k < n$,
so the strong induction hypothesis is [vacuously true](sets.qmd#def-vacuous-truth),
and the proof for $n = n_0$ is a
[base case](proof-writing.qmd#def-proof-by-induction).
When the proof for $n$ needs particular earlier cases
that do not exist for the first few $n$,
those few cases are shown separately as further
[base cases](proof-writing.qmd#def-proof-by-induction).

:::
